name: Maximum Subarray
description: You are given an array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$, consisting of $$$n$$$ integers. You are also given two integers $$$k$$$ and $$$x$$$. You have to perform the following operation exactly once: add $$$x$$$ to the elements on exactly $$$k$$$ distinct positions, and subtract $$$x$$$ from all the others. For example, if $$$a = [2, -1, 2, 3]$$$, $$$k = 1$$$, $$$x = 2$$$, and we have picked the first element, then after the operation the array $$$a = [4, -3, 0, 1]$$$. Let $$$f(a)$$$ be the maximum possible sum of a subarray of $$$a$$$. The subarray of $$$a$$$ is a contiguous part of the array $$$a$$$, i. e. the array $$$a_i, a_{i + 1}, \dots, a_j$$$ for some $$$1 \le i \le j \le n$$$. An empty subarray should also be considered, it has sum $$$0$$$. Let the array $$$a'$$$ be the array $$$a$$$ after applying the aforementioned operation. Apply the operation in such a way that $$$f(a')$$$ is the maximum possible, and print the maximum possible value of $$$f(a')$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ and $$$x$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$0 \le k \le \min(20, n)$$$; $$$-10^9 \le x \le 10^9$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$). The sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer — the maximum possible value of $$$f(a')$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1796D — Maximum Subarray [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
